usual_baseline: Risks listed incompletely. Procedure-specific risks documented in 31–42% [1368, 1388]. Average 56.6% of BOA risks per hip fracture form [1479]. Death recorded in 40–49% of hip fracture forms [1366, 1439]. Abbreviations in 38–54% [1368, 1396]. COVID-19 risk on 41–49% of forms [1159, 1162, 1166]. Consent Form Four next-of-kin section completed in 30% [1401].
fix_that_works: Hip fracture consent form or risk stickers: 100% of risks documented [1334]; 56.6% to 87.9% [1479]. Procedure-specific Orthoconsent form read at home: understanding 57% to 81% [1238]. M&M, email and stickers: abbreviations 54% to 22% [1396]. Teaching: side/site 76.4% to 97.5% [1400]; procedure-specific risks 42% to 76% [1388]. Infographic: COVID-19 risk 49% to 70% [1166].
fix_that_fails: Three loops of teaching and a displayed risk list never reached 100%; mortality fell to 21% and dislocation stayed at 14% [1366]. Written information fell from 14% to 8% [1388]. Copy offered to patient fell to 8% when stickers ran out [1368]. Poster and awareness: elective COVID-19 risk only 41.7% to 48.9% [1162]. Feedback: allograft consent 38% to 56% [1313].
consultant_advice: Hip fracture consent forms are overdone and the fix is always a procedure-specific form or sticker. Don't repeat it. Measure what the patient understood, as [1238] did, whether they got written information, or best-interests decisions and next-of-kin involvement for patients lacking capacity [1401].
